AccountExport.description:
Self-service data export — GDPR/DSGVO Art. 15/20 style 'what do you
have about me' response. Deliberately does not include raw telemetry
file contents (those are downloadable separately if needed) — this is
the structured data the DB actually holds about the driver.
AccountExport.title: AccountExport

AdminDriverOut.description:
GET /admin/drivers — includes email, unlike every public/driver-
facing schema in this project (DriverProfileOut, DriverLookupOut):
this endpoint is gated by the operator admin token, a different and
higher trust boundary than a driver's own session, and an admin
plausibly needs it for a support/moderation contact. Never returned
from anything a driver or the public can reach.
AdminDriverOut.title: AdminDriverOut

AdminLapReportOut.description:
GET /admin/reports — the moderation view, with enough about the
reported lap and reporter to actually judge the report without a
second round-trip per row.
AdminLapReportOut.title: AdminLapReportOut

AdminLapSummary.description:
Enough to actually judge a lap without a second round-trip — used
both standalone (GET /admin/laps/{id}) and nested in LapReportOut.
AdminLapSummary.title: AdminLapSummary

AdminReviewDecision.description:
V0.9.3 — POST /admin/laps/{id}/review: the admin's decision on a lap the
track-limits check could not decide on its own.
AdminReviewDecision.title: AdminReviewDecision

AppSessionResponse.description:
POST /accounts/app-session (V0.9.2): a web session for the desktop app's
analysis window. Unlike LoginResponse this DOES carry the raw session token —
the caller is the desktop client, already holding a stronger credential (its
own auth token), and it hands the token straight to its own window, which
turns it into the usual HttpOnly cookie via /accounts/app-session/activate.
AppSessionResponse.title: AppSessionResponse

CatalogVenueOut.description:
One track with all of its layouts/variants (V0.8.9). `layouts` is empty
for a known track nobody has driven yet — it is still listed, so every
track exists in the UI before its first lap.
CatalogVenueOut.title: CatalogVenueOut

DesktopLoginRequest.description: POST /accounts/desktop-login (V1.0) — the desktop client's "Connect" with email + password.
DesktopLoginRequest.title: DesktopLoginRequest

DesktopLoginResponse.description:
The desktop client's credentials. The auth token is NEW (the previous one stops working —
only one PC is connected at a time); the client secret is the account's existing one.
DesktopLoginResponse.title: DesktopLoginResponse

DiscordLinkStatusOut.description:
GET /accounts/discord — deliberately just a flag. The Discord user
id itself is never sent to the browser (nothing there needs it).
DiscordLinkStatusOut.title: DiscordLinkStatusOut

DisplayNameUpdateRequest.description:
PATCH /accounts/me — the name shown on leaderboards, profiles, teams and
in Discord. Until V0.8.9 it was fixed at registration (whatever was typed
into the 'New driver' box, even a throwaway "Test") and could never change.
DisplayNameUpdateRequest.title: DisplayNameUpdateRequest

DriverActivityItem.description:
One entry in a driver's public recent-activity list. Same shape as
TeamActivityItem (both reuse RecordEvent, no separate activity-log
table) but kept as its own schema — this is a per-driver view, not
scoped to any one team's membership.
DriverActivityItem.title: DriverActivityItem

DriverLookupOut.description:
GET /drivers/lookup?display_name=... — the minimal, privacy-safe
primitive team invitations need (resolve a known display name to a
driver_id) without building a full driver directory/search feature.
Never includes email or anything else private — display_name is
already public (leaderboards, team member lists).
DriverLookupOut.title: DriverLookupOut

DriverPersonalRecordOut.description:
One row in a driver's public personal-bests list — their own best
*valid* lap for a given (track, car_model), same grouping
records.py's PR/WR logic already uses (car_model, not car_name —
ignores livery/team/number).
DriverPersonalRecordOut.title: DriverPersonalRecordOut

DriverProfileOut.description:
GET /drivers/{id}/public (§4). Deliberately excludes: email,
password_hash, auth_token/client_secret, session data, is_locked —
none of those fields are even queried for this endpoint, let alone
returned (see routers/drivers.py).
DriverProfileOut.title: DriverProfileOut

warning.default: Dev-only credential issuance. auth_token and client_secret are shown once, here, and not stored anywhere retrievable — save them now. Replace this endpoint with real account/key management before launch.
warning.title: Warning

DriverTeamOut.description:
A team a driver publicly belongs to — id/name/role only, never the
team's invite_code (that's a credential, not public information).
DriverTeamOut.title: DriverTeamOut

LapReportOut.description:
Response for a driver's own POST /telemetry/laps/{id}/report — just
confirms what they filed. See AdminLapReportOut for the enriched
admin-review shape (different endpoint, different audience).
LapReportOut.title: LapReportOut

LegalInfoOut.description:
GET /legal (V1.0) — what the legal pages fill in: the operator (from .env; null when not
configured), the minimum age, the version of the terms and whether anybody may sign up.
LegalInfoOut.title: LegalInfoOut

LoginResponse.description:
No auth_token here (V0.7.2) — login's credential is an HttpOnly
session cookie the browser holds automatically, not a value the
frontend needs to see or store. See server/sessions.py.
LoginResponse.title: LoginResponse

RaceRules.description:
What a race prescribes. Everything optional except what makes the calculator work at
all; values the admin does not know stay empty and the calculator says so instead of
assuming them.
RaceRules.title: RaceRules

RecentActivityEntry.description:
GET /leaderboard/recent (V0.7.2 landing page) — the most recent
valid laps platform-wide. Same trust level as the leaderboard itself
(public, driver names already shown there) — nothing new is exposed,
just a different, time-ordered slice of the same Lap data.
RecentActivityEntry.title: RecentActivityEntry

warning.default: Shown once, not stored anywhere retrievable — save it now, then run `python -m client.main --reconfigure` to update the desktop client. Your old secret stopped working immediately.
warning.title: Warning

warning.default: Shown once, not stored anywhere retrievable — save it now. Your old token stopped working immediately.
warning.title: Warning

SessionOut.description:
One row in Account Settings → Sessions (spec §3.9). Deliberately
excludes the session token itself (obviously) and anything about the
desktop client's auth_token/client_secret — those aren't sessions in
this sense, see server/sessions.py.
SessionOut.title: SessionOut

SetPasswordRequest.description:
POST /accounts/set-password — attach email+password to an existing
(token-only) driver identity, or change the password on one that
already has them. Deliberately the same endpoint for both: the
server can already tell them apart (email already set or not) and a
driver shouldn't need to remember which flow applies to them.
SetPasswordRequest.title: SetPasswordRequest

SignupRequest.description:
POST /accounts/signup (V1.0) — the website's sign-up form: driver name, email, password, and
the two confirmations the terms require. Creates the account WITH email and password (the
desktop client then signs in with them, POST /accounts/desktop-login), so nobody has to copy
tokens any more.
SignupRequest.title: SignupRequest

TeamActivityItem.description:
One entry in the team's activity console — reuses RecordEvent,
no separate activity-log table.
TeamActivityItem.title: TeamActivityItem

TeamDetail.description:
Team-Übersicht — every number computed live from Lap/RecordEvent,
nothing artificially stored (per the explicit requirement: don't add
counter columns, derive from existing data).
TeamDetail.title: TeamDetail

TeamInvitationCreateRequest.description:
POST /teams/{id}/invitations. Addressed by driver_id, not a name
or email — see models.TeamInvitation's docstring for why. The web UI
resolves a display name to a driver_id first via GET
/drivers/lookup, same as any other caller would.
TeamInvitationCreateRequest.title: TeamInvitationCreateRequest

TeamRecordOut.description:
One row per (track, car_model) the team has a valid lap on — the
team's current best there. Derived live from Lap, same principle as
the rest of the leaderboard system (no CurrentRecord table).

your_lap_time/gap (V0.7.2 §21 "You vs Team") are None when the
caller has no valid lap of their own on this exact (track,
car_model) — not 0.0, which would misleadingly read as "you tied the
record". you_hold_it is true exactly when the caller IS the
record-holder (driver_name matches them), in which case gap is 0.0.
TeamRecordOut.title: TeamRecordOut

TeamStatsOut.description:
GET /teams/{id}/stats?window=... (V0.7.2 §9.4) — same shape as
TeamDetail's fixed-window fields, but for a caller-selected window
instead of the hardcoded 14/7-day ones there (which stay as-is for
backward compatibility, see that endpoint).
TeamStatsOut.title: TeamStatsOut

WhoAmIOut.description:
GET /accounts/me — the only thing missing before V0.7.2's dashboard
rework: a way to resolve "my own driver_id" from just a valid
credential (bearer token OR session cookie), for the one case that
didn't already have it — a session restored from a pasted-in
auth_token (see web/js/pages/auth.js), which never learns driver_id
any other way. Deliberately minimal — this is identity resolution,
not a profile; DriverProfileOut (the public one) already covers
"everything about a driver" for driver_id once known.

email/email_verified (V0.8-NAS §2) stay within that same "who am I"
spirit rather than becoming a second endpoint — Account Settings
needs exactly this to show a verify-email prompt.
WhoAmIOut.title: WhoAmIOut

post.description:
The desktop client's "Connect" with email + password (V1.0). Issues a NEW auth token —
the previous one stops working, so one PC is connected at a time (connecting a second PC
disconnects the first; it says so and offers "Reconnect account…") — and returns the
account's existing client secret, so laps already waiting on this PC still upload. Same
generic failure as /login (no hint which emails have accounts).

delete.description:
Removes the Discord link (idempotent — unlinking when nothing is
linked is a harmless 200) and cancels any pending link code.

post.description:
Email+password sign-in. Creates a web session (server/sessions.py)
and sets it as an HttpOnly cookie — completely separate from the
desktop client's Bearer auth_token (see that module's docstring for
why: V0.7.0's first version of this endpoint reused
_issue_fresh_token(), which overwrote drivers.token_hash and silently
disconnected a driver's running LMU client on every web login — a
real bug, not a hypothetical one). No token is returned in the
response body; the browser holds the session via the cookie alone.

Deliberately generic on failure ("Invalid email or password") whether
the email doesn't exist, has no password set, or the password is
wrong — distinguishing those would let an attacker enumerate which
emails have accounts. is_locked is checked and reported distinctly
(403, not 401) — get_current_driver already does the same for
token-based auth, so this isn't a new information leak, just the
existing convention applied here too.

Ends the CURRENT web session only (see logout_all for every
device). A no-op, not an error, if there's no session cookie to begin
with — logging out twice, or logging out a bearer-token-only client
that never had a cookie session, shouldn't 401.

Revokes every web session for this driver (all browsers/devices
signed in via email+password) — but deliberately NOT the desktop
client's auth_token/client_secret, a separate credential domain with
its own revoke (POST /accounts/revoke). Works whether the caller is
currently authenticated via cookie or via the bearer token, since
get_current_driver resolves either to the same driver.

delete.description:
Self-service full account deletion — driver, laps, telemetry files,
record events, team memberships, discord link, and any lap reports
they filed. Irreversible; no confirmation step here because the web
UI is expected to confirm before calling this (see web/js/pages/account.js).

The cascade itself lives in server/driver_lifecycle.py (shared with the
admin endpoint; V0.8.7 completed it — it used to miss several tables,
which made this endpoint fail with a 500 on PostgreSQL).

V0.7.2: refuses (409) to proceed if the driver owns a team that still
has other members — deleting the account would otherwise silently
leave that team without an owner. A solo-owned team (this driver is
the only member) is deleted along with the account; a team with other
members must be explicitly transferred (POST
.../transfer-ownership) or deleted by its owner first — see
server/team_lifecycle.py's resolve_owned_teams_before_driver_deletion
for why this isn't done automatically here.

get.description:
Resolves the caller's own identity from whichever credential they
presented (desktop bearer token or web session cookie — see
server/auth.py). See WhoAmIOut's docstring for why this needed to
exist.

patch.description:
Rename yourself. Everything that shows a driver's name reads it from the
driver row at display time (leaderboards, profiles, teams, invitations,
Discord announcements), so the new name appears everywhere at once — old
laps and records are not rewritten because they never stored the name.
Names are not unique (as at registration); blank or whitespace-only names
are rejected.

get.description:
Self-service data export (DSGVO Art. 15/20-style 'what do you have
about me'). Returns the structured DB data — driver profile and lap
records. Deliberately does not inline raw telemetry file bytes (those
would make this response arbitrarily large); the telemetry_path on
each lap is server-internal only and not exposed here.

post.description:
Always returns 200/ok, whether or not that email belongs to an
account with a password set — a response that varied by that would
let anyone probe which emails are registered. The actual email (if
any) is sent as a side effect, not reflected in the response.

Immediately invalidates the current auth token — every client using
it (web session, desktop app, Discord link) is signed out on its next
request. If this driver has no email/password set (see set_password
below), this is terminal for the identity: there's no way back in via
the desktop client afterwards — that specific credential is dead for
good, so use this for "this token is compromised, kill it now" (lost
device, leaked token), not for routine rotation, where rotate-token
above is the one to use instead (issues a new token without cutting
off access). A driver WITH a password set is NOT locked out of the
WEB app by this, though: POST /accounts/login (V0.7.2) still works —
it grants access via its own, fully independent session cookie (see
server/sessions.py), never by reviving this token.

Issue a new client_secret (the HMAC signing key used by the desktop
client) for the authenticated driver. Run `python -m client.main
--reconfigure` afterwards to save the new secret locally.

Issue a new auth token for the authenticated driver and invalidate
the old one immediately. Use this if a token may have leaked, or on a
routine rotation schedule — no need to re-register (which would create
a brand-new, disconnected driver identity).

get.description:
Account Settings → Sessions (spec §3.9): every currently-valid web
session for this driver, so they can spot one they don't recognize
and revoke it. Does NOT include the desktop client's auth_token — that
isn't a "session" in this sense (see sessions.py's module docstring),
and it's a single fixed credential, not a list of them.

schema.title: Response List Sessions Accounts Sessions Get

delete.description:
Revoke one specific session by id (the "this doesn't look like me"
button next to a row in the Sessions list) — as opposed to
logout-all's blanket revoke. Scoped to the caller's own driver_id so
one driver can't revoke another's session by guessing ids.

post.description:
Attach email+password to a token-only driver identity, or change
the password on one that already has them (see SetPasswordRequest's
docstring for why both share one endpoint). This is what turns a
driver from "recoverable only by keeping the auth_token safe" into
"recoverable via POST /accounts/login and password-reset" — see
revoke_token's docstring above.

The website's sign-up form (V1.0): one step instead of register → copy token and secret →
set email and password. Creates the account with email and password, records the accepted
terms (server/routers/legal.py TERMS_VERSION), sends the verification email and signs the
browser in (session cookie, like /login). The desktop client connects with the same email
and password (POST /accounts/desktop-login) — no token to copy.

Public (no auth) — the link in the email is the proof, same as
password-reset confirm. Rejects a token whose captured `email` no
longer matches the driver's current email (see
EmailVerificationToken's docstring): confirming a stale token from
before a later email change must verify nothing.

Re-sends the verification link for the driver's CURRENT email.
404s if there's no email set at all (nothing to verify) rather than
silently succeeding — that's a real usage error the Account Settings
UI shouldn't need to guess about. Already-verified is not an error
either — it's the answer, sent back as a plain 200 status the
frontend already checks.

get.description: The audit log, newest first, filtered by lap, kind or request id.

schema.title: Response Audit Events Admin Audit Get

get.description: Recomputes the whole audit chain (server/audit.py). ok=false names the first broken row.

schema.title: Response Audit Verify Admin Audit Verify Get

get.description:
What the server has learned about car models (server/car_identity.py): every
alias with how often the game confirmed it, conflicts (two models reported for one
veh_filename group — never used), and how the laps' identities were decided.

schema.title: Response Car Identity Overview Admin Car Identity Get

get.description:
Database vs telemetry files (server/consistency.py). Read-only: the repairs are
scripts/consistency_check.py's, behind explicit flags.

§15 driver moderation needs a way to find a driver at all — there
was no listing/search endpoint anywhere in the API before this one.
Substring, case-insensitive (unlike GET /drivers/lookup's exact-match
requirement — that endpoint is reachable by any signed-in driver and
deliberately can't become a searchable directory; this one is gated
by the operator admin token, a categorically different trust level).
Includes email — see AdminDriverOut's docstring for why that's fine
here specifically.

schema.title: Response List Drivers Admin Drivers Get

delete.description:
Same cascade as the self-service DELETE /accounts/me — see that
endpoint's docstring for the FK-ordering reasoning. This is the admin
equivalent for e.g. GDPR/DSGVO erasure requests submitted outside the
web UI (support email, etc.), or removing a banned cheater's data.

V0.7.2: same team-ownership guard as the self-service endpoint —
blocked (409) by default if this driver owns a team with other
members. Unlike self-service, an admin can pass ?force=true to
auto-transfer ownership to the next-earliest-joined member instead: a
banned cheater won't come back to transfer it themselves, and an
admin acting on a support/GDPR request needs a way to actually finish
the deletion.

schema.title: Response Delete Driver Admin Drivers  Driver Id  Delete

post.description:
Blocks all future authenticated requests from this driver
(get_current_driver checks is_locked) without touching their existing
data or revoking+losing the token the way self-service revoke does —
reversible via /unlock.

schema.title: Response Lock Driver Admin Drivers  Driver Id  Lock Post
Response Unlock Driver Admin Drivers  Driver Id  Unlock Post

get.description:
Quarantined laps (what was found, when, with which request id), how many laps are signed
with the current key, and the audit chain head. A full check of every file:
scripts/integrity_check.py (docs/RUNBOOKS.md).

schema.title: Response Integrity Overview Admin Integrity Get

get.description:
The "View" action on a report, or standalone lap lookup for direct
moderation outside of any report (§15's "Lap moderation: View,
Invalidate").

post.description:
Checks one lap's file now (full hash, no cache). A failure quarantines the lap (if it is
not yet); with release=true a quarantined lap whose file verifies again returns to the state it
had before (review status kept from then).

schema.title: Response Verify Lap Integrity Admin Laps  Lap Id  Integrity Post

patch.description:
Soft-invalidate a lap: flips is_valid to False with a recorded
reason. Deliberately does NOT delete the row or its RecordEvents —
per the architecture decision (see records.py), leaderboards and
records are derived live from Lap.is_valid, so this alone removes the
lap from leaderboards/records on the next query. No CurrentRecord
table to reconcile, no re-computation step needed.

schema.title: Response Invalidate Lap Admin Laps  Lap Id  Invalidate Patch

post.description:
clear: the lap stays valid and leaves the queue. invalidate: same effect as
PATCH /laps/{id}/invalidate (leaderboards and records follow live), with the
review's findings as the reason.

V0.9.9: clearing a HELD lap makes it official — its record events (PR / WR / TEAM_BEST,
Discord) are evaluated now, against the laps that count at this moment, under the same lock
as an upload. A quarantined lap cannot be cleared here: its file must verify first
(POST /admin/laps/{id}/integrity). Every decision is written to the audit log.

schema.title: Response Review Lap Admin Laps  Lap Id  Review Post

get.description:
Uploads of the last `hours`: per outcome, failure rate, the most common reasons, durations,
per client version, the latest failures (each with its request id — the same id is in the
server log and the client's X-Request-ID response header). Plus the analysis cache.

schema.title: Response List Reports Admin Reports Get
Response Resolve Report Admin Reports  Report Id  Resolve Post

get.description:
Laps the check (server/track_limits.py, server/lap_decision.py) flagged for a human look.
Each entry carries the verdict with every finding (what, where on the lap, which signal).

V0.9.9: "pending" lists every lap waiting for a decision — "held" (REVIEW: not official until
cleared) and the older "pending" ones (counting provisionally, flagged before V0.9.9).
"held" / "quarantined" (integrity failures, see GET /admin/integrity) list only those.

schema.title: Response Review Queue Admin Review Get
Response List Rule Sets Admin Rule Sets Get
Response Delete Rule Set Admin Rule Sets  Rule Set Id  Delete

get.description:
V0.9.3.1: every track-limits rule with its tier (LMU verdict / Garage16 rule /
heuristic), its effect and whether its meaning is confirmed — plus which heuristics this
server lets invalidate (LMU_GARAGE_TRACK_LIMITS_INVALIDATING; default: none).

schema.title: Response Track Limits Rules Admin Track Limits Rules Get

get.description:
Exact, case-insensitive match only — deliberately never a fuzzy or
partial-substring search, which would make this a de facto searchable
driver directory (a bigger privacy/product surface than "resolve a
name I already know exactly"). display_name has no uniqueness
constraint (see models.py), so this can return more than one match —
that's the caller's (or the inviting UI's) problem to disambiguate,
not something to silently pick the "first" of.

schema.title: Response Lookup Driver By Display Name Drivers Lookup Get

get.description:
Public, unauthenticated — same trust level as the leaderboard
itself (which already names this driver on every lap they've set).
Every field here is something already visible elsewhere in the
public API (leaderboards, team member lists); this just collects it
into one place per driver, per §4.

Checks DB connectivity (a plain SELECT 1), not just "the process is
alive" — a process that's up but can't reach its database should fail
an orchestrator's healthcheck, not report 'ok'. Also reports version
info so a client (or a human) can tell if the server has moved past
what a given desktop client expects.
The process answers — nothing else checked (a restart is the only cure when this fails).

schema.title: Response Health Live Health Live Get

get.description:
Can this server do its job right now? 200 = yes, 503 = no (with which part is missing).

Required: the database answers, the telemetry storage exists and is writable. Reported but
NOT failing: a running backup (uploads wait a moment, reading works), little free disk space
(a warning below LMU_GARAGE_DISK_WARN_FREE_MB, default 2048), optional integrations.

Every invitation addressed to the caller, across all teams, most
recent first — including past accepted/declined/expired/revoked ones
(a short history is more useful than "pending only" and costs nothing
extra to include).

schema.title: Response My Invitations Invitations Mine Get

get.description:
Sub-leaderboard: best valid lap per driver for this exact track +
car model, ignoring team/livery/car number (those live in car_name,
not car_model — see server/models.py).

schema.title: Response Car Leaderboard Leaderboard Car  Track Name   Car Model  Get

get.description:
Every car_model with at least one uploaded lap — optionally scoped
to one track and/or one class. The car_class filter (V0.7.2 §9.5) is
what makes a real three-level cascade possible (Track → Class →
Model, each narrowed by everything picked before it) instead of
Model only ever being narrowed by Track — without it, picking
"Hypercar" at Le Mans still offered every GT3 model driven there too.
See catalog_classes for the same NULL-exclusion note.

schema.title: Response Catalog Cars Leaderboard Catalog Cars Get

get.description:
Every class, always (V0.8.9): the six known LMU classes exist before any
lap is driven, plus any other class LMU has sent, each with its number of
valid laps (at `track_name` when given). The UI can then offer the whole
list and just say "no laps yet" instead of hiding classes nobody drove.

schema.title: Response Catalog Class Options Leaderboard Catalog Class Options Get

get.description:
Every car_class with at least one uploaded lap — optionally scoped
to one track, which is what the leaderboard UI actually wants (no
point offering a class nobody's driven at the selected track).
car_class is NULL for laps from clients older than V0.6.3; those are
excluded here the same way they're already excluded from the
leaderboard itself.

schema.title: Response Catalog Classes Leaderboard Catalog Classes Get

get.description: Every track_name with at least one uploaded lap, alphabetical.

schema.title: Response Catalog Tracks Leaderboard Catalog Tracks Get

get.description:
Every track — grouped by venue, with ALL layouts/variants LMU has sent
(V0.8.9). No manual list to maintain:

  - venues come from a seeded list (server/catalog.py), so a known track
    is listed even before its first lap (`layouts` empty, `lap_count` 0);
  - layouts are exactly the raw track strings found in uploaded laps, so
    every variant appears by itself the first time someone drives it;
  - a track we've never heard of is its own venue — it shows up too.

`q` searches the venue name, its keywords and its layout names, ignoring
case, accents and punctuation: q=fuji returns Fuji Speedway with every
Fuji layout. Only valid laps count (the leaderboards only show those).

schema.title: Response Catalog Venues Leaderboard Catalog Venues Get

get.description:
Main leaderboard: best valid lap per driver for this track, across
every car model within `car_class` (e.g. all Hypercars together,
regardless of manufacturer).

schema.title: Response Class Leaderboard Leaderboard Class  Track Name   Car Class  Get

get.description:
Most recent valid laps platform-wide, newest first — the landing
page's "recent activity" section (V0.7.2). Deliberately simple: no
per-driver dedup, no filtering by class/car — just what's actually
been happening lately, same spirit as a team's activity console but
across the whole platform instead of one team.

schema.title: Response Recent Activity Leaderboard Recent Get

post.description:
DEPRECATED ALIAS (V0.8.7) of POST /accounts/discord/link-code, kept
so nothing that still calls the old path breaks. It does not belong
under /teams — it links a driver's own Discord account — and shares the
exact same implementation, including the "already linked" 409.

schema.title: Response My Teams Teams Mine Get
Response Delete Team Teams  Team Id  Delete

get.description:
Recent PR/WR/TEAM_BEST events among this team's drivers — the
"Konsole" — reuses RecordEvent, no separate activity-log table.

schema.title: Response Team Activity Teams  Team Id  Activity Get

get.description:
Every invitation this team has ever sent, most recent first —
owner/admin only (the invited driver's own name is visible to
everyone on the team already via the member list once accepted; this
view additionally shows who's pending/declined/revoked, which is
exactly the "who have we already asked" question a manager needs
answered before inviting more people).

schema.title: Response List Invitations Teams  Team Id  Invitations Get

post.description:
Only valid for a pending or already-expired invitation — a nudge,
extending the deadline (and reviving an expired one back to pending).
Deliberately NOT usable on a declined or revoked invitation: reviving
a decision the driver (or the team) already explicitly made would be
surprising. Send a brand-new invitation instead for that case — a
fresh, deliberate ask rather than a silently resurrected old one.

schema.title: Response Team Car Leaderboard Teams  Team Id  Leaderboard Car  Track Name   Car Model  Get

get.description:
Same as /leaderboard/class/..., scoped to this team's own drivers
only — reuses the exact ranking logic (see leaderboard_ranking.py).

schema.title: Response Team Class Leaderboard Teams  Team Id  Leaderboard Class  Track Name   Car Class  Get

get.description:
V0.7.2: rewritten from N queries-per-member (3 queries × member
count) to a fixed small number of queries regardless of team size —
one membership+driver fetch (eager-loaded, so display_name doesn't
trigger a lazy-load per row either) plus one GROUP BY aggregate query
each for lap count, PB count, and last activity, merged in Python.
Same response shape and values as before — see
tests/test_v0_7_2_phase1.py for both the query-count bound and a
3-member correctness check (each member's own driver, not the
caller's).

schema.title: Response Team Members Teams  Team Id  Members Get

delete.description:
A member may always remove themselves (leave). Otherwise: owner can
remove admins/members; admin can remove members only. The owner can
never be removed this way — transfer ownership or delete the team
instead, so a team is never left without an owner.

schema.title: Response Remove Member Teams  Team Id  Members  Target Driver Id  Delete

post.description:
Owner-only: promote a member to admin, or demote an admin back to
member. Setting "owner" here is deliberately rejected by the request
schema's pattern — use /transfer-ownership for that, which also
demotes the previous owner in the same operation.

get.description:
The team's current best on every (track, car_model) combo it has a
valid lap on — derived live from Lap, same principle as the rest of
the leaderboard system (no stored "current record" table). Also
computes the caller's own gap to each (V0.7.2 §21 "You vs Team") —
see TeamRecordOut's docstring for the None-vs-0.0 distinction.

schema.title: Response Team Records Teams  Team Id  Records Get

get.description:
V0.7.2 §9.4 — the same four numbers as TeamDetail's fixed-window
fields (laps/PBs/active drivers), but for a caller-chosen window
(today/7d/30d/all) instead of TeamDetail's hardcoded 14- and 7-day
ones. Deliberately a separate endpoint rather than replacing
TeamDetail's fields — those stay exactly as they were for anyone
already depending on that response shape; this is additive.

"today" is the trailing 24 hours, not "since local midnight" — the
server has no notion of the caller's timezone, and a rolling window
is simpler to reason about (and to test) than a calendar-day one that
would silently depend on whichever timezone happened to be used.

Every channel the analysis can show, grouped, with unit and label.

Static and the same for everyone, so — unlike everything else here — it may be
cached publicly. The ETag is derived from the content, so it changes exactly
when the catalog does.

Track cards: every venue with all its layouts, lap/driver counts, the
fastest valid lap and the classes driven there. Built entirely from uploads
(plus the seeded venue list) — nobody enters a track by hand. Public: it only
contains what the leaderboards show anyway. The outline of a layout is a
separate call (it has to read a telemetry file).

schema.title: Response Circuits Telemetry Analysis Circuits Get

get.description:
The shape of a layout, taken from its fastest valid lap that has position
data (no stored track files to maintain; a layout nobody has driven has no
outline). Includes the lap length and, when known, the sector boundaries.

schema.title: Response Circuit Outline Telemetry Analysis Circuits Outline Get

get.description:
Two laps (or one, when lap_b is omitted) on a common distance grid.

Response, in short:
  grid        {start, step, count} — distance in metres; point i is at start + i*step
  laps        {a, b} headers (driver, car, lap time, sectors ...); + c, d (V0.9.4)
  delta       seconds, A minus B, null without lap_b; positive = A is behind
  time        {a, b} seconds since lap start at each grid point
  channels    {key: {label, unit, group, discrete, fixed_range, a, b}} — a/b are
              value lists, or null when that lap's file lacks the channel
  recording   {a, b}: {level: "full"|"basic", client_version, channels_available,
              channels_total} — "basic" = recorded by a client older than 0.9.0,
              so only the basic channels exist for that lap
  unavailable channel keys missing in at least one of the laps
  map         {x_a, y_a, x_b, y_b, mirrored, ...} plan view, Y up, same frame for both;
              V0.9.4: offset_b (Lap 2's line vs Lap 1's, m, inside = +) and side
              (direction of the nearest corner, +1 left / -1 right)
  sectors     {a: [d1, d2], b: [...]} distances of the sector boundaries
  orientation how each lap's sign conventions were decided (for transparency)
  corners     V0.9.1 corner table; V0.9.4 adds braking/throttle details and phases
  extra_delta V0.9.4, with `extra`: {c: [...], d: [...]} each extra lap minus the reference
  analysis_version  version of the computation (V0.9.1, additive)

How much data is sent (V0.9.1): only the requested channels are read and
returned; `max_points` bounds the points per series (the grid is widened to
fit — the raw data in the file is untouched); `start`/`end` return just a
stretch of track, at the same or a finer `step`, for zoom-in refinement. Without
these parameters the response is what V0.9.0 returned.

Caching: the numeric part is cached in memory (server/analysis_cache.py), keyed
by the laps' content hashes, the channels and the grid parameters. Permissions
are checked first, every time. The response carries an ETag; a repeat request
with If-None-Match gets 304 without recomputing anything.

get.description:
The corners of the same driver's EARLIER valid laps on the same layout with the same car
model, as stored at upload (server/lap_insights.py "corners": [apex, braking point, min
speed, full-throttle point, exit speed] per corner). From the database only — the coach
compares a corner of Lap 1 with how the driver usually drives it ("in 4 of your last 5
laps ..."). Another driver's laps: valid laps only, like everywhere.

schema.title: Response Corner History Telemetry Analysis Corner History Get

get.description:
Histograms of channels over the whole lap — the share of the lap's TIME in each
bin, both laps on the same bins. The classic use is the damper histogram (damper
velocity per wheel: bump/rebound and low/high-speed shares, `knee` mm/s being the
split), but any catalog channel works (gear = time per gear, tyre temperatures, ...).

Small response (a few dozen numbers per channel and lap), cached like /compare.

The driver's laps, fastest first — the valid ones, plus invalid ones when
the driver asks about themselves. Optionally for one track and car model.

schema.title: Response Driver Laps Telemetry Analysis Drivers  Driver Id  Laps Get

get.description:
What happened where on the lap: the track-limits findings the server stored at
upload (server/track_limits.py — LMU's own flags, wheels off, beyond the edge, ...)
and the wheel events measured from the telemetry (lock-ups and wheelspin per wheel).
Every event has its lap distance, so the views can mark it and jump to it.

Sector times of every lap of the SESSION this lap belongs to (same grouping as the Stint
Analyzer), the fastest DRIVEN sector of the session and of all the driver's valid laps on this
layout and car model — each with the lap it comes from — and this lap's potential per sector
(its sector minus the best). The sum of best sectors is a calculated figure, labelled so.

schema.title: Response Lap Sectors Telemetry Analysis Lap Sectors Get

get.description:
A lap's header plus which catalog channels its file actually contains
(laps recorded before V0.9.0 only have the basic ones).

schema.title: Response Lap Info Telemetry Analysis Laps  Lap Id  Get

get.description:
V0.9.7 — how trustworthy this lap's recording is (server/telemetry_health.py): channels,
samples, gaps, time/distance only forward, distance-axis anchoring, speed vs lap distance,
duration vs lap time, implausible jumps, the resolution of a braking point — plus the lap's
validation verdict next to it. The file part is cached by the file's content hash.

V0.9.4 — the driven lines of a stretch at high resolution, for the zoomed track map.

Only positions (+ Lap 2's lateral offset from Lap 1, inside = +, and the inside direction)
— no channels — on a fine grid (default 0.5 m, at most LINE_MAX_POINTS points; the step is
widened to fit). The mirror decision and the corner directions come from the WHOLE laps,
so the detail lies exactly on the overview. Same permissions, caching and ETag as /compare.
  -> {grid, x_a, y_a, x_b, y_b, [x_c, y_c, x_d, y_d], offset_b, side, mirrored}

"You vs ..." in one call — nobody has to look up two lap ids.

Lap A: your best valid lap on `track_name` (optionally for one car model) — for
mode=my_best your most RECENT valid lap instead, compared with your best.
Lap B: the reference of `mode` for lap A's track and car (see /reference).
Used by "You vs Garage16 Best", "You vs Team Best", "You vs My Best" and the
circuit library's "Compare my lap with it". Nothing found => found=false and a
reason, never a made-up pairing. Without `track_name` the viewer's most recent
valid lap decides track and car.

schema.title: Response Quick Compare Telemetry Analysis Quick Get

get.description:
The lap to compare `lap_id` with.

  kind=wr         fastest VALID lap by anyone on the same track layout and car
                  (records.py's WR rule). Garage16 has no official world record:
                  this is the fastest lap on Garage16, shown as "Garage16 Best".
  kind=team_best  fastest valid lap among everyone who shares a team with you
  kind=my_best    your own fastest valid lap
  scope           "model" (same car, default) or "class" (same car class)

`found` is false — with a `reason` code and no lap — when nothing suitable exists;
a different lap is never substituted. If the best lap IS `lap_id`, it is not
offered again: `already_best` is true and `lap` is the next-fastest, or null.
The lap being viewed must be one the viewer may open.

get.description:
Your sessions (stints): consecutive laps on one track, car and session type
without a pause longer than 15 minutes — with robust consistency figures (median,
spread of the clean laps, how many within 0.5 s of the best), the lap-time trend over
the stint, and fuel / virtual energy / tyre wear per lap. Your own laps only.

schema.title: Response Driving Sessions Telemetry Analysis Sessions Get

get.description:
You and your team mates on one track (and car model): valid laps only, robust figures
(median of the clean laps, spread, best), consumption and wear per lap (medians).

schema.title: Response Team Comparison Telemetry Analysis Stints Drivers Get

get.description:
The race rule sets an admin defined; with track_name, the ones for that track and the
general ones (no track) — for the strategy calculator.

schema.title: Response Rule Sets Telemetry Analysis Stints Rule Sets Get

get.description:
One session (the one this lap belongs to): every lap with its flags, the stints, the pit
stops, the tyre sets and the session's figures — see server/stints.py.

schema.title: Response Stint Session Telemetry Analysis Stints Session Get

get.description:
The sessions of a driver (you, or a team mate: valid laps only), newest first, each with
the id of its last lap (the key to open it), and the drivers you may look at.

schema.title: Response Stint Sessions Telemetry Analysis Stints Sessions Get

get.description:
A driver's theoretical best on a layout with one car model: the fastest time over
every PROFILE_STEP_M stretch, taken from their VALID laps, summed — plus the simpler
sector-based ideal (best S1 + S2 + S3). A CALCULATED figure: stretches of different
laps, never driven as one lap.

V0.9.3.1 — track conditions are not mixed silently: laps are grouped as dry / mixed /
wet (share of the lap on a wet surface, server/lap_insights.py) or unknown (older laps
without that signal). `conditions=auto` uses the group of the driver's fastest lap;
every other group is reported with its lap count, never folded in. `all` mixes them on
request (and says so). Grip level and track temperature are reported as a spread.

From the database only (the per-lap profiles are stored at upload), so it costs no
file reads. Another driver's figure uses their valid laps only, like everything else.

schema.title: Response Theoretical Best Lap Telemetry Analysis Theoretical Best Get

get.description:
V0.9.5 — asphalt, both edges and the kerbs of the layout, in the map's coordinates.

Built from LMU's path_lateral / track_edge / surface type of the laps on the map plus up to
SURFACE_EXTRA_LAPS recent valid laps of the same layout (only geometry is returned — nothing
about those laps or their drivers). -> {"surface": {...} | null, "mirrored", "reason"}; null when
the laps were recorded without these fields (client < 0.9) or the data cannot be read reliably —
"reason" says which (V0.9.9.3; null when there is a surface).

schema.title: Response List My Laps Telemetry Laps Get

post.description:
Any authenticated driver can flag a lap as suspicious. Purely
advisory: it does not change is_valid by itself — an admin reviews
reports via GET /admin/reports and acts (invalidate the lap, or mark
the report resolved with no action) through the admin router.

V0.9.7: every attempt is recorded (server/upload_log.py) — outcome, reason, request id,
lap id, duration — for the operations view; the log line carries the same ids.
